name: Change in an accounting estimate, and how it differs from a change in accounting policy
definition: An accounting estimate is an approximation used where an item cannot be measured with precision. Revising it because circumstances changed, or because of new information, more experience or subsequent developments, is a change in accounting ESTIMATE — not an extraordinary item and not a prior period item. Its effect is recognised in the period of the change, and also in future periods if the change affects them, using the same classification previously used for the estimate. Where it is difficult to distinguish a change in policy from a change in estimate, AS 5 requires it to be treated as a change in ESTIMATE, with appropriate disclosure.
why_it_exists: This is the load-bearing fork for any system that posts corrections. A policy change and an estimate change look alike on the face of a document but carry different treatment: policy change means restating the presentation and disclosing the quantified impact; estimate change means recognise it now and going forward, with no prior period item and no restatement. AS 5 paragraph 22 removes the tie by naming the default.

Prior period items are generally infrequent in nature and can be distinguished from changes in accounting estimates. Accounting estimates by their nature are approximations that may need revision as additional information becomes known. For example, income or expense recognised on the outcome of a contingency which previously could not be estimated reliably does not constitute a prior period item.
